testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should happen before air pressure in an air brake system tank drops below 55 psi?

options.text: The warning light should turn on.
The vehicle will not shift out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The warning light should turn on.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light must turn on before the air pressure drops below 55 psi. If the warning light does not work during an inspection, the vehicle is not safe to drive.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air, what does this mean?

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if the pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong with the system and a mechanic should check it.

questions.question: Air brakes use ____ to work.
questions.explanation: Air brakes use compressed air to work properly.

questions.question: When braking on dry pavement at 55 mph, how much distance does brake lag add to your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to the total stopping distance.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air, what does this mean?

options.text: Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if the pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong with the system and a mechanic should check it.

questions.question: The emergency brake system is made up of ____.

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system
Only parts of the service brake system
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three brake types: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts of both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997, must have anti-lock brakes. Other vehicles with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1998, must also have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: The ____ between an air compressor and reservoir tank stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is placed between the air compressor and the first main reservoir. It stops air from escaping the system if the compressor develops a leak.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Pull out the air brake knob.

questions.explanation: To make a normal stop with air brakes, press the brake pedal down.

questions.question: An emergency brake must be controlled by:
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency and parking brakes. Since air pressure can leak away, these brakes must be held in place by mechanical force.

questions.question: Why do some air brake systems add alcohol to the system?

options.text: To stop the brakes from squeaking.
To prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
To keep people from breathing air from the system.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to stop ice from forming when it is cold.

questions.question: When do you need an air brake endorsement?

options.text: To drive a vehicle with air brakes.
To drive any truck with a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: To drive a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: You must pass an air brakes knowledge test to get a license to drive a vehicle with air brakes. This includes air over hydraulic braking systems.

questions.question: What does an air compressor governor control?

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the air storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.

questions.question: Which item is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems include an air compressor, governor, storage tanks, drains, alcohol evaporator, safety valve, brake pedal, foundation brakes, pressure gauges, warning signals, stop light switch, brake limiting valve, spring brakes, and parking brake controls. An air filter is not part of the system.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, what happens if one air system loses pressure?

options.text: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There is usually no noticeable effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully if one air system loses pressure. If this happens while driving, pull off the road and park as soon as you can.

questions.question: What prevents wheels from locking up when you brake?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheels from locking up when the brakes are applied.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most newer heavy-duty trucks use?
questions.explanation: Most newer heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. A dual system has two separate air brake systems that share one set of brake controls.

questions.question: In a static leakage test, a triple combination vehicle with air brakes should not leak more than ____ in one minute.
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test, a triple combination vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 5 psi in one minute. If it leaks faster, the vehicle needs repair and should not be driven.

questions.question: What color are ABS malfunction lamps?
questions.explanation: ABS malfunction lamps are usually yellow. If the ABS does not work, the regular brakes will still work.

questions.question: When parking, when should you NOT use the parking brake?

options.text: When the brakes are very hot.
When the brakes are very cold.
When there is snow on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake if your brakes are hot after going down a steep hill. Let your brakes cool first, or you may damage them.

questions.question: While driving, ____ holds spring brakes in place.
questions.explanation: Air pressure holds spring brakes in place while you drive. If air pressure drops too low, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you should:

options.text: Lower the windows in the cab.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when leaving your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: When operating a vehicle with a dual air brake system, you should:

options.text: Warm up the vehicle before driving to get fuel to the engine.
Let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
Start driving right after the vehicle starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems. Watch the air pressure gauges to check the pressure levels.

questions.question: On flat surfaces, wheel chocks:

options.text: Can prevent a parked vehicle from moving.
Make a parked vehicle easier to roll.
Should only be used on the front driver's side tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can prevent a parked vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: When you cannot use a parking brake, wheel chocks can hold a parked vehicle in place on a level surface.

questions.question: To keep normal stopping power, drivers with a front brake limiting valve should:

options.text: Set the control to the off position.
Set the control to the neutral position.

questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have front brake limiting valves with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Setting the valve to "slippery" reduces stopping power. Keep the valve set to "normal" for full stopping power. Front wheel brakes work well in all driving conditions.
